**Result**
- **2252-1: passed QC.** Readings at the five QC points were 62–63 µm (limit 55–85), and the camera found no runs or bare areas. At that rate a single lid takes about 160–200 ml, so three lids need 460 ml or more, against 320 ml in the pot. The job couldn't be finished from one pot even with perfect settings.

My own mistake made it worse. I sprayed the first coat on lid 1 at the default settings plus a 50 mm overspray margin, which wasted about 76 ml for 16 µm. - Plan about 200 ml of paint per lid.

# Spray booth SB-2 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with an air-assisted spray gun fed from the paint pot. It sprays raster passes: horizontal
  lines `pitch` mm apart over a rectangle of a panel, extended by `margin` mm past it on every side.
- Panel rack: the enclosure lids of job J-2252 (2252-1, 2252-2, 2252-3), 450 x 450 mm, degreased and ready. Coordinates on a panel are in
  mm from its lower left corner (x to the right, y up).
- Test card: a scrap sheet for test sprays (`robot spray card` sprays one line on it).
- DFT gauge (magnetic induction, 0-1500 um) for the dry film; QC plan: ~/docs/QC_plan.md.
- Paint: one pot of alkyd enamel AK-3 (RAL 2004 orange); `paint status` shows the level and the lot certificate.
- Station logbook: ~/LOGBOOK.md.

## Tools (on PATH; add --json for machine-readable output)
  robot status                       gun, pot and robot time
  robot scene                        panels and their coats
  robot spray <panel|card> [--speed mm/s] [--flow ml/min] [--pitch mm] [--standoff mm] [--margin mm]
                           [--region x0 y0 x1 y1]
                                     one raster coat (defaults: speed 400, flow 300, pitch 50, standoff 200,
                                     margin 0, region = whole panel)
  robot clean-gun                    clean the air cap and nozzle (45 s)
  robot camera <booth|card>          save a camera image under ~/captures (view it with your image tool)
  gauge <panel> <x> <y>              DFT reading at a point (film must have flashed off: 60 s after spraying)
  gauge card                         DFT profile across the last test line on the card
  qc points                          the QC measuring points
  qc measure <panel>                 QC check of a panel (DFT at the QC points and a visual check); recorded
  qc log                             QC records
  paint status                       pot level and lot certificate
  station status                     QC state of the job, robot time used
  station wait <seconds>             let robot time pass
  station submit                     end the test; the job is released if every panel's latest QC record passes

**Result**
- **2252-1: passed QC.** Readings at the five QC points were 62–63 µm (limit 55–85), and the camera found no runs or bare areas. I also checked the gauge at extra points, including the edges and outer corners: they read 58–67 µm, so the film is in spec over the whole panel, not just at the QC points.

Only about 10–15 % of the sprayed paint ended up on the panel. One full coat, about 62–76 ml, built only 16–22 µm of dry film. At that rate a single lid takes about 160–200 ml, so three lids need 460 ml or more, against 320 ml in the pot. The job couldn't be finished from one pot even with perfect settings.

My own mistake made it worse. I sprayed the first coat on lid 1 at the default settings plus a 50 mm overspray margin, which wasted about 76 ml for 16 µm. After testing on the card I moved the gun closer (100 mm instead of 200 mm) and cut the margin to 25 mm, which built more film per ml. I should have run those tests before spraying a panel.

**Next steps**
- Coat 2252-2 and 2252-3 when more AK-3 arrives on Monday. Settings that worked on lid 1: three coats at standoff 100 mm, margin 25 mm, pitch 50 mm, flow 300 ml/min, speed 340–400 mm/s.
